text.p: Former England captain Mike Gatting had the satisfaction of handing out some punishment to his 1993 Ashes tormentor Shane Warne at Lord's on Saturday.
Gatting, now an England selector, made 85 playing for Middlesex, who were all out for 305 on the first day of the three-day match against Australia.
Having overcome the wizardry of leg-spinner Warne in what must surely be his last match against the Australians, the 40-year-old Gatting was yorked by strike bowler Glenn McGrath.
McGrath, the eight-wicket destroyer of England's first innings in the rain-hit second test at Lord's, was too quick for Gatting's drive with the second delivery of a new spell.
Gatting, memorably the victim of Warne's magical first ball in the 1993 Ashes series which pitched outside leg stump and hit the off stump, batted for 200 minutes and faced 156 deliveries.
The ex-England skipper struck six of his 15 fours at Warne's expense, and shared a third wicket stand of 120 in 212 balls with Mark Ramprakash.
Middlesex captain Ramprakash scored 76 in 166 minutes and 140 balls, stroking 10 fours, and a six off Warne.
Gatting then added 72 in 25 overs for the fourth wicket with 18-year-old Owais Shah (28), who toured Australia with England's A team in the 1996-97 season.

Middlesex were eventually prised out just before the end of the day, McGrath returning four for 61 and Warne one for 76 in his first serious bowl since flying back from a brief return trip to Australia.
